Category-constrained predictive mean matching with sensitivity replacement

Source: R/imputer.R
mice.impute.catmech_threshold_corruption.Rd

A univariate imputation method for an exactly coarsened continuous variable. Missing values and declared threshold conflicts are reconstructed. An observed, flagged value that agrees with its category is reconstructed with the supplied sensitivity probability and otherwise retained exactly.

Usage

mice.impute.catmech_threshold_corruption(
  y,
  ry,
  x,
  wy = NULL,
  ...,
  category,
  bounds,
  flag = NULL,
  flag_yes = "Yes",
  corruption_probability = NULL,
  original_y = y,
  trusted = NULL,
  min_donors = 1L,
  n_donors = 5L,
  fallback = c("error", "normal")
)

Arguments

y

Numeric working response, as supplied by `mice`.

ry

Logical vector identifying originally observed responses available for fitting. Flagged and category-inconsistent observations are excluded regardless of this vector.

x

Numeric predictor matrix with one row per response. All entries must be finite; use a zero-column matrix for an intercept-only model.

wy

Logical vector identifying cells to complete or reconstruct. Defaults to `!ry`. All missing values and all threshold conflicts must be selected.

...

Additional arguments supplied by `mice`, such as predictor types.

category

Observed category labels, one per row, with no missing values.

bounds

Named list with one entry per category. Each entry contains scalar numeric `lower` and `upper` endpoints and scalar logical `lower_inclusive` and `upper_inclusive` flags.

flag

Optional quality flags, one per row. Missing flags do not mark a value as suspect; this is a substantive trust assumption.

flag_yes

Label that marks a suspect observation.

corruption_probability

Sensitivity replacement probability for flagged, observed, in-bound values, as one number or one number per row in `[0, 1]`. It is not an estimated or posterior probability of measurement error. Must be explicit when flag is supplied; NULL means zero only without flags.

original_y

Original response before any imputation or reconstruction. Pass an immutable copy when using this method inside `mice`.

trusted

Optional logical mask restricting the fitting and donor sample. It cannot admit flagged, missing, or category-inconsistent observations.

min_donors

Minimum number of eligible donors required to use predictive mean matching for a recipient.

n_donors

Number of nearest eligible donors from which to sample.

fallback

Policy when fewer than `min_donors` are available: `"error"` (default), or an explicitly requested truncated `"normal"` draw.

Value

A numeric vector containing only the `wy` cells, in row order. Its `audit` attribute is a data frame with the original row, reason, reconstruction decision, actual change, donor row, fallback use, and eligible donor count. For a missing original value, `changed` is `NA`.

Details

The fitting model uses a rank-reduced Gaussian linear regression with the usual reference-prior variance and coefficient draws. Donor distances compare fitted donor predictions with drawn recipient predictions (type-1 matching). Rank reduction is allowed only when reconstructed recipients satisfy the same predictor dependencies as the trusted fitting rows; otherwise prediction is unidentified and the method errors. A positive residual degree of freedom and positive residual variance are required whenever reconstruction is requested. A degenerate model produces an error, rather than an invented residual variance.

Donors always come from original, trusted observations in the recipient's category. The method never falls back to contaminated observations. Sparse donor support and model misspecification can still invalidate inference. Constrained PMM and the retain/replace rule do not establish proper multiple imputation or valid confidence-interval coverage. Study those properties for the intended analysis. The normal fallback is a stronger extrapolation assumption and is recorded in the audit.
